2607.05563.title: From Graphs to Gradients: Physics-Inspired Structural Attribution for Cyber-Physical IoT Systems and Beyond
2607.05563.paper_summary: Interpretable explanation methods in Artificial Intelligence aim to uncover the underlying causes and their effects, enabling a deeper understanding of why a system behaves in a certain way under different inputs. Unlike traditional explainability methods, which mainly highlight correlations between input and output variables, causal explanation focuses on interventional questions. By doing so, it provides more robust insights, helping users understand automated decisions, especially in high-risk domains. Recovering an explicit directed causal structure, however, is often impractical in large-scale, hybrid cyber-physical systems with feedback loops and partial observability. This paper introduces a novel framework inspired by statistical mechanics that instead models variable dependencies through an undirected, energy-based representation of cyber-physical IoT systems. Our approach enables rigorous dependency-aware attribution by analysing how variations in the energy landscape reflect the influence of individual components, without recovering a directed causal graph. It also supports reasoning about perturbation effects across hybrid interactions, providing reliable explanations of abnormal behaviours. We empirically examined our framework through simulations on an industrial IoT testbed with hybrid continuous and discrete variables, demonstrating higher attribution accuracy, improved robustness and better scalability than state-of-the-art graph-based approaches. While the attributions are not intended to fully recover the system's generative dynamics, they provide valuable, dependency-aware explanations supporting both human interpretation and downstream predictive and diagnostic tasks. Although demonstrated in industrial IoT security, our framework also applies to other high-dimensional cyber-physical and socio-technical systems requiring principled, structural explanations.
2607.05563.paper_summary_zh: 可解釋的人工智慧解釋方法旨在揭示潛在原因及其影響，使人們更深入地理解為何系統在不同輸入下以特定方式行為。與傳統的可解釋性方法主要強調輸入與輸出變數之間的相關性不同，因果解釋則專注於干預性問題。這樣做提供了更穩健的見解，幫助用戶理解自動化決策，尤其是在高風險領域。然而，在具有反饋迴路和部分可觀察性的龐大混合網路物理系統中，恢復明確的有向因果結構通常是不切實際的。本文介紹了一種受統計力學啟發的新框架，該框架通過無向的、基於能量的表示來建模網路物理物聯網系統中的變數依賴性。我們的方法通過分析能量景觀的變化如何反映個別組件的影響，實現了嚴謹的依賴性意識歸因，而無需恢復有向因果圖。它還支持對混合互動中擾動效應的推理，提供對異常行為的可靠解釋。我們通過在具有混合連續和離散變數的工業物聯網測試平台上進行模擬，實證檢驗了我們的框架，顯示出比最先進的基於圖的方法更高的歸因準確性、更好的穩健性和更佳的可擴展性。雖然這些歸因並不旨在完全恢復系統的生成動力學，但它們提供了有價值的、依賴性意識的解釋，支持人類解釋以及下游的預測和診斷任務。儘管在工業物聯網安全中得到了驗證，我們的框架也適用於其他需要原則性結構解釋的高維網路物理和社會技術系統。
